Now that these chemicals are treated as non-energy products, their inputs are changed to mass amounts and the energy shares have to be re-balanced among NG, electricity and MeOH.  Below is the copy of the emai messagel from Jeongwoo Han for reference:

For the transesterification process (BD production), use the following assumptions.
Total Energy Inputs (Btu/lb. of BD): 1,213
Shares of Process Fuels: NG 30.7%; Electricity 4.6%; MeOH 64.7%
Other chemical (lb/lb of BD): Sodium hydroxide 0.000972; Sodium methoxide 0.023105; Hydrochloric acid 0.043376; Phosphoric acid 0.000999; Citric acid 0.000729
 
We have sodium hydroxide, hydrochloric acid and phosphoric acid, but no sodium methoxide and citric acid.
For sodium methoxide, use methanol as a surrogate. For citric acid, don? put an upstream.

Both Methanol input contains CO2 input emission ratio of 137.5% (C ratio of methanol/C ratio of CO2=0.375/12*44)
The Methanol in upper input box is actually sodium methoxide; methanol in group input is methanol.

name: Methanol Feedstock Selection
notes:
Methanol production depending on the feedstock and conversion process selected. The order of methanol in "Drag and Drop Inputs Below" dialog box follows the following order:

1) 50% Clean Pine and 50% Logging Residue
2) 100% Logging Residue
3) Switchgrass
4) Miscanthus
5) Corn Stover

For example, if you want to see results for methanol produced from switchgrass only, fill up the third one's quantity as 1 mmbtu, and leave the rest as 0. 

Users can hover over the icons beside "Methanol" to see which feedstock was used to produce each entry.
